angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 523,925 km at 86.05 pc = 0.08 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 11.6209 +/- 0.0163 mas (same row, RUWE 1.10): 86.05 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.75309 solar radii from Lafarga et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-6699 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.548ag512L/abstract): 523,925 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.747 (0.707 to 0.795) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4705.1 K from Lafarga et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-6699 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.548ag512L/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Lafarga et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-6699 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.548ag512L/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-6699.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.557, rounded to two decimals
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, TYC 9105-1214-1: main object type PM*, High Proper Motion Star
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-6699 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.59732, from TICv8 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....158..138S/abstract)
ageSource: Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 6450063790712030336, flags_flame 00: age_flame 12.839461 Gyr (16th to 84th percentiles 5.821908 to 13.5)
rotationPeriodMeasuredSource: Measured in this project from the TESS mission's own 2-minute light curves of sectors 101, 102, 103 and 104 (packages/telescope-cli/src/archives/tess/reduce.mts), by the method and criteria of Holcomb et al. (2022, ApJ 936, 138): 14.58 d, the light swinging by 0.28% as the star turns

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
